articles.title: 11 年纪录就此中断，索尼发行游戏无缘今年 TGA 年度游戏奖提名
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据外媒 VGC 报道，索尼发行的游戏自 2015 年以来首次无缘 TGA 年度游戏奖提名，持续 11 年的提名纪录就此中断。原本最有希望角逐年度游戏奖的作品之一《漫威金刚狼》虽然获得了总体正面的评价，但口碑仍不及失眠组此前的作品。该作最终获得两项提名，分别是利亚姆 · 麦金泰尔凭借“金刚狼”一角入围最佳表演奖，以及游戏本身入围无障碍创新奖。索尼旗下另外两款作品《沙罗周期》和《失落星船：马拉松》也各获一项提名，分别入围最佳动作游戏奖和最佳多人游戏奖。尽管失去了年度游戏奖提名，PlayStation 在本届 TGA 仍获得 9 项提名，是提名数量最多的发行商之一，与 Annapurna Interactive 并列第三，仅次于卡普空和任天堂。PlayStation 与 XBOX 的提名数量差距也因此缩小。XBOX 本届共获得 8 项提名，仅比 PlayStation 少一项。回顾过去 11 年的年度游戏奖评选，索尼发行的作品曾三次夺得最高奖项。IT之家汇总索尼历年来入围年度游戏奖的作品：2015 年：《血源诅咒》，最终输给 CD Projekt 的《巫师 3：狂猎》。2016 年：《神秘海域 4：盗贼末路》，最终输给暴雪的《守望先锋》。2017 年：《地平线：零之曙光》，最终输给任天堂的《塞尔达传说：旷野之息》。2018 年：《战神》，最终获奖；《漫威蜘蛛侠》也获得提名。2019 年：《死亡搁浅》，最终输给《只狼：影逝二度》。2020 年：《最后生还者第二部》，最终获奖；《对马岛之魂》也获得提名。2021 年：《瑞奇与叮当：时空跳转》，最终输给 EA 的《双人成行》。2022 年：《战神：诸神黄昏》和《地平线：西之绝境》，最终输给万代南梦宫的《艾尔登法环》。2023 年：《漫威蜘蛛侠 2》，最终输给拉瑞安工作室的《博德之门 3》。2024 年：《宇宙机器人》，最终获奖。2025 年：《死亡搁浅 2：冥滩之上》，最终输给 Kepler Interactive 的《光与影：33 号远征队》。索尼今年仍有机会在其他奖项上有所斩获。《沙罗周期》角逐最佳动作游戏奖，《漫威斗魂》角逐最佳格斗游戏奖，《失落星船：马拉松》角逐最佳多人游戏奖，《战神：劳菲》角逐最受期待游戏奖；《漫威金刚狼》则同时角逐无障碍创新奖和最佳表演奖。

articles.title: MUFG: Reverse Yankees Are About 20% of Europe Corporates
articles.content: MUFG EMEA Capital Markets Co-Head Fabianna del Canto says the percentage of reverse yankees, or debt issued by US companies in foreign currencies, has ballooned to around 20% of the European corporate market, with clients now looking to issue further afield markets like Australia's. She joins Bloomberg's Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson on "The Opening Trade" ahead of Bloomberg's annual Global Credit Forum today in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 曝英特尔启动新一轮裁员，波及全球 IT 部门
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（18 日）上午报道，过去两年接连经历多轮裁员后，英特尔又开始新一轮人员削减，此次裁员波及公司的全球 IT 部门。CEO 陈立武推动英特尔精简组织、压缩规模的工作仍在继续，年底前也没有停下来的迹象。本周，英特尔全球 IT 部门有员工在社交媒体上发文，透露自己被裁的消息。英特尔发言人在一份声明中解释说，公司将持续审视人员配置，确保员工和资源能够集中到最重要的业务上，以配合提高运营效率、聚焦核心业务的整体战略。IT之家从报道中获悉，英特尔没有透露此次裁员的具体人数，也未说明涉及哪些团队。此次裁员是英特尔持续推进重组的又一步。过去几年，公司在制造业务上屡遭挫折，并在 AI 芯片市场不断丢失份额。为了扭转局面，英特尔持续缩减人员规模、收缩项目，今年还进行了数轮小规模裁员。陈立武去年出任英特尔 CEO 后，便着手推动公司重组。他此前透露，这项计划的主要目标是降低成本、精简管理层级，并减少对优先级较低项目的投入。英特尔提交的公司文件显示，截至今年 9 月底，员工人数为 81100 人，而 2025 年底为 85100 人。英特尔员工规模自 2024 年以来持续大幅收缩。2024 年，时任 CEO 帕特 · 基辛格曾宣布裁员计划，拟削减超过 15000 个岗位，相当于当时员工总数的约 15%。

articles.title: 消息称荣耀明年没有常规大折叠手机，取而代之的是阔折叠
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，博主 @旺仔百事通 今日发文透露，荣耀明年没有常规大折叠手机，取而代之的是阔折叠手机。有网友称看不懂荣耀的战略，因为国内大折叠手机市场，荣耀排名第二（华为排名第一）。他认为荣耀应该保持优势，再发一小部分阔折叠探探路。博主表示：“在没有卖到绝对的数量之前，折叠屏都是不赚钱的。”据IT之家此前报道，博主 @数码闲聊站 今年 9 月曾爆料，荣耀也有阔折叠手机，搭载 2nm 骁龙新芯片，排期 2027Q1，希望能赶到春节前发布。根据该博主此前爆料，荣耀阔折叠搭载骁龙 8 Elite Gen6 系列处理器，主屏测试 7.6 英寸 ±、副屏 5.5 英寸 ±。作为参考，华为今年 4 月发布了行业首款横向阔折叠手机 Pura X Max，内外屏均采用了≈√2:1 的类纸比例设计，外屏尺寸为 5.4 英寸，内屏尺寸 7.7 英寸，售价 10,999 元起。今年 9 月，华为常务董事、产品投资评审委员会主任、终端 BG 董事长余承东宣布该机上市四个月发货量突破 120 万台。另外，小米 18 Fold“中折叠”手机搭载 5.38 英寸外屏 + 7.58 英寸内屏，集结了玄戒 O3 AI 旗舰 SoC（首发）、新一代小米澎湃 OS 4 系统、Xiaomi MiMo 端侧大模型等核心亮点，已于 9 月 7 日正式发布，售价 10,999 元起。苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 则于 10 月 23 日发售，国行定价 15,999 元起。该机采用书本式内折设计，闭合时外屏为 5.4 英寸、展开后内屏为 7.6 英寸，搭载台积电 2nm 工艺的 A20 Pro 芯片，宣称持续性能较 iPhone 17 Pro 提升最多 35%。

articles.title: 海韵预告：PRIME ENTERPRISE PX-3200 电源即将上市
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，海韵 (Seasonic) 近日发布预告，宣布其面向工作站等高性能本地计算系统打造的 PRIME ENTERPRISE PX-3200 电源即将上市。根据该企业在今年度的 COMPUTEX 2026 台北国际电脑展上的展示，PRIME ENTERPRISE PX 系列的三款高功率产品均符合 ATX12V 3.1、PCIe CEM 5.1 规范，获得 80 PLUS 与 Cybenetics 铂金能效认证。其导入服务器级验证，符合服务器 EDPP 高动态负载测试标准，采用高精度电压调节技术；可提供至多 6 组 12V-2×6 输出；内置 120mm 台达滚珠轴承风扇；具备 OPP、OVP、UVP、SCP、OCP、OTP 安全防护。

articles.title: 理想汽车 CTO 谢炎台积电 OIP 论坛开讲，解读马赫 M100 从技术到应用全流程
articles.content: 2026 年 11 月 17 日，台积电 OIP（Open Innovation Platform，开放创新平台）生态系统论坛在北京举行。作为全球半导体设计、EDA、IP 及封装测试领域最具影响力的年度技术盛会之一，本届论坛汇聚了芯片架构、AI 计算与系统创新方向的顶尖企业与专家。理想汽车首席技术官谢炎受邀发表主题演讲，成为本次论坛唯一的特邀演讲嘉宾，理想汽车也成为台积电 OIP 生态系统论坛举办以来首家进行特邀演讲的大陆企业。谢炎演讲的题目为《高效 AI 推理系统的设计思考与实践》，核心内容围绕理想汽车自研的马赫 M100 芯片展开。从架构设计到量产装车，这颗芯片完整走过了从原创技术到规模化应用的全流程。马赫 M100 是全球首款量产的动态数据流架构 AI 芯片，采用 5 纳米车规级工艺，单颗算力达 1280 TOPS。与市面上多数仅服务于自动驾驶的专用芯片不同，它定位为面向 AI 时代打造的端侧推理芯片 —— 已跑通车上所有智能化场景，既能运行大语言模型、支撑智能体应用，也能驱动智能辅助驾驶，并为未来更多 AI 场景预留空间。目前马赫 M100 已量产交付，搭载于全新理想 L9、全新理想 L8、新一代理想 L6、新一代理想 MEGA、全新理想 i9 和 2026 款理想 i6 等车型。马赫 M100 最核心的突破，在于动态数据流架构。这是一种与冯 · 诺依曼架构截然不同的计算机体系结构，核心理念是 " 数据驱动 " 而非 " 指令驱动 "。理想汽车 2022 年启动芯片设计时就判断，仅仅造出一颗更快的芯片解决不了行业根本矛盾。摩尔定律与登纳德缩放定律双双放缓，AI 算力需求却从深度学习革命到 Agent 时代持续暴增。冯 · 诺依曼架构统治计算行业七十年，大量晶体管用于缓存、调度和分支预测等管理开销，面对 AI 的海量并行计算效率难以提升。AI 计算天然是并行的，数据是张量，关系确定，流动路径清晰。基于这一判断，理想汽车选择让数据的流动直接驱动计算，让架构围绕 AI 的计算形态来设计。来到 AI 推理场景，这一架构体现出三项核心优势。数据直达减少搬运浪费，数据在计算单元间直接传递，省去频繁往返内存的中转；流水线式高效执行，多个计算单元同时运转，大幅缩短推理耗时；全局广播能力，片内高速总线可将同一份数据一次送达多个计算单元，提升并行效率。三者叠加，让马赫 M100 把绝大部分硬件资源用于实际计算而非调度开销。马赫 M100 选择动态数据流路线，在保持高效率的同时具备完整可编程性，AI 算法迭代时只需重新编译适配，硬件无需更换。软硬一体联合设计也是马赫 M100 的核心竞争力。芯片和算法从一开始就紧密配合，而不是各自开发最后再凑在一起。理想汽车内部团队完全了解自身产品的需求方向和长期规划，能在芯片定义之初就做出最精准的技术判断。今年，理想汽车基座模型团队还和国创决策智能技术研究所联合研发了端侧大语言模型的软硬协同设计定律，用数学方法让芯片与算法的协同更加高效严谨。当然，技术领先还需要落实在用户体验上。2026 年 11 月 6 日，理想汽车推送 OTA9.2 版本，马赫 VLA 2.5 正式上线，其中最受关注的就是全新的 3D ViT 感知模型。3D ViT 即三维视觉 Transformer 编码器，被看作理想具身智能技术体系中的 " 眼睛 "。过去的视觉感知好比隔着 2D 屏幕看世界，需要从平面画面推断三维空间；3D ViT 在编码阶段就融合了 3D 空间几何与语义信息，让模型同时理解物体的位置、类别及彼此的空间关系。它的前向感知距离达到 300 米，等效 1080 线分辨率，动态视力提升 50%。具体到用户层面，马赫 VLA 2.5 带来了倒车礼让功能，在施工绕行、动物避让、盲区通行和防御性驾驶等场景中也有更拟人的表现。3D ViT 能够在车端大规模落地，背后正是马赫 M100 芯片的支撑。理想汽车上一代算力平台受限于内存带宽和数据搬运效率，无法原生支持 3D ViT。依托马赫 M100 的动态数据流架构，这一模型才得以搬上车端。马赫 M100 的技术价值已经在多个维度得到验证。2026 年初，理想汽车马赫 M100 芯片论文入选 ISCA 工业分区，理想汽车是自该分区设立以来全球首家入选的汽车企业。资本市场同样给出积极回应，2026 年 10 月，理想汽车芯片子公司马赫心完成首轮融资，融资金额 16.25 亿元，融资后最大估值达 171 亿元。总体来说，马赫 M100 正在经历一个从技术突破到用户价值再到行业认可的完整循环。对于理想汽车而言，马赫 M100 的意义不止于一颗算力芯片，它代表着一家汽车企业在底层计算技术领域的深度布局，也为智能汽车的算力底座提供了一种全新的可能。

articles.title: 贝索斯：把科技巨头当替罪羊，并不能解决美国经济问题
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，亚马逊创始人杰夫 · 贝索斯认为，大型科技公司已经成了美国新的众矢之的。他批评政客习惯于寻找替罪羊，而不是着手解决经济问题的根源。当地时间 17 日，贝索斯在 Semafor 举办的“Silicon Valley & The World”大会上接受采访时表示，寻找替罪羊是由来已久的政治手法，虽然有利于政治操作，却根本解决不了问题。在贝索斯看来，公众对不同行业的态度一直在变化：律师、华尔街、房东都曾成为批评对象，现在轮到了科技巨头们。他认为，外界将整个科技行业描绘成反派并不符合事实。“房东有时会被塑造成反派，现在轮到大型的科技公司了，整个科技行业都成了反派。但这种形象并不准确，也不符合事实。我认为，科技行业的大多数人只想埋头做好自己的工作，这个行业里并没有多少所谓的恶行。”贝索斯发表上述言论之际，大型科技公司正面临越来越多的公众质疑，其影响力已经延伸到日常生活的方方面面。例如，大型数据中心可能推高当地公共事业费用，Flock 的车牌识别摄像头网络等 AI 监控工具也引发了隐私争议。隐私保护、能源开支以及 AI 对就业的冲击，正不断加剧公众对科技巨头扩张的抵触情绪。民众对生活成本的强烈不满，也与这些担忧交织在一起。战争推高燃油和部分消费品价格，住房成本又长期居高不下，种种经济压力，影响了美国选民在 2026 年中期选举中的投票选择。

articles.title: 腾讯 WorkBuddy 日活跃用户数超 1000 万，成为中国大语言模型日均 Token 用量最高 AI 产品
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，腾讯今日发布 2026 年第三季度财报，截至 11 月初，WorkBuddy 日活跃用户数超过 1000 万，日均 Token 调用量超过 100 万亿，成为中国大语言模型日均 Token 用量最高的 AI 产品。官方表示，自今年 3 月发布以来，WorkBuddy 已完成 100 多个大版本更新。开放平台上线两个月以来，Buddy 应用已覆盖 55 个专业场景、超 30 个垂直领域，包括金融、法律、医疗、教育、公益、设计、SaaS 等。IT之家获悉，目前 WorkBuddy 企业版已落地 50 多个行业，覆盖中国企业 500 强中的 50%。模型方面，Hy4 flash 上线首日 Token 调用量已突破 50 万亿，创混元系列模型首日调用量新高，并登顶 OpenRouter LLM 日排行榜，成为全球开发者高频调用的首选轻量模型之一。在 WorkBuddy 中，Hy4 flash 上线首日的调用量也达到 Hy4 preview 上线首日的 10 倍。相关阅读：《腾讯控股 2026 年前三季度归母净利润 1777.27 亿元，同比增长 7%》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，华为官方今日继续揭秘首款「逻辑折叠」技术 τ 芯片 —— 麒麟 9050 系列更多配置信息，今日最新公开了新一代芯片级安全架构的情报。据介绍，麒麟 9050 系列芯片是首批获权威检测的抗量子攻击移动 SoC，也是首个芯片级隐私安全平台，支持 MSP 安全处理器与 eSE 安全芯片双芯协同，并获 CCRC EAL5+ 安全认证。IT之家了解到，麒麟 9050 系列进一步增强了芯片级安全能力，支持后量子密码相关安全功能；此外，它还是首个芯片级隐私安全 SoC 平台，通过移动安全处理器与独立安全芯片协同，可为启动安全、数据安全、隐私保护和通信安全提供底层支撑。值得一提的是，下一代麒麟 2027 芯片已经就绪。华为半导体业务无线终端芯片产品管理部部长徐松余表示，到目前为止，所有的测试结果都符合预期，因此在未来 10 年（逻辑折叠）的演进是可持续的。至于具体到哪个阶段，每个点需要用什么样的技术，可能需要逐步再开展和讨论。相关阅读：《华为麒麟 9050 系列芯片配备新一代显示 DPU，支持全彩 AI-HDR2020》《华为麒麟 9050 系列芯片智能音视频处理情报公开：低延迟 AI 异构协同计算、率先支持 H.266 解码》《华为麒麟 9050 系列芯片新一代巴龙 AI Modem 情报公开：首创融合通信架构、业界首发四卡三待》《华为麒麟 9050 系列新马良 GPU、AI ISP 情报公开：实装二代硬件光追，首次实现 2 亿像素融合拍照》《华为麒麟 9050 系列芯片新一代灵犀 CPU 详细信息公开：9 核 16 线程并行调度，支持内存压缩加速》《华为麒麟 9050 系列芯片官宣搭载新一代达芬奇架构 NPU，业界首个 30B MoE 大模型入端》《首款「逻辑折叠」技术 τ 芯片：华为详解麒麟 9050 系列核心升级，晶体管密度暴涨 53.5%》

articles.title: 黄仁勋离职风波引发诉讼风险：英伟达高管有保险，公司自身却未投保
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据路透社报道，英伟达（Nvidia）为公司高管和董事购买了保险，以应对证券诉讼可能带来的个人责任风险，但公司自身却没有购买相应保险。这意味着，如果围绕黄仁勋突然辞去 CEO 职务而引发的诉讼最终胜诉，英伟达可能不得不动用现金储备承担相关赔偿。The Insurer 上周六报道称，英伟达为公司高管和董事购买的保险，最高赔付额度达到 9.5 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 63.46 亿元人民币）。不过，英伟达并未购买通常用于承担公司在证券诉讼中辩护费用、和解金及法院判决赔偿金的企业责任保险。这意味着，如果英伟达董事或高管因未能妥善履行公司监督职责而承担个人法律责任，保险公司可以根据保单条款，支付英伟达无法代为承担的合规和解金或判决赔偿，从而保护相关人员的个人资产。但如果针对英伟达公司的证券欺诈诉讼胜诉，涉及股价暴跌的赔偿则需要由公司自行承担。英伟达目前持有超过 500 亿美元（现汇率约合 3,339.93 亿元人民币）的现金储备。上周四，黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）辞去了英伟达 CEO 职务。此前，他在一份声明中承认自己对妻子不忠。本周二，黄仁勋表示，他对给英伟达董事会带来的麻烦深感遗憾，并称如果有机会重返公司，自己将深感荣幸。不过，英伟达董事会并未考虑让他回归。英伟达等公司通常会为董事和高管提供法律赔偿保障。不过，根据美国特拉华州公司法，企业不能为董事和高管承担某些类型的法律索赔责任，因此公司通常会通过购买保险来覆盖这部分风险。与绝大多数美国上市公司不同，英伟达的特殊之处在于，其没有购买针对公司自身证券欺诈责任的保险。两位保险行业专家认为，英伟达雄厚的财务实力可能是公司选择不为自身企业责任购买保险的原因。保险及风险管理公司鲍德温集团（The Baldwin Group）旗下 CAC 公司的财务险业务执行副总裁兼负责人里克 · 戈伊顿（Rik Goyton）表示：“英伟达的资产负债表规模甚至超过了许多保险公司，因此可以合理推断，该公司认为，市场提供的风险转移保险方案并没有足够的价值，没必要为此投保。”已有两起诉讼提起自 11 月 8 日黄仁勋承认对妻子不忠以来，针对英伟达及相关人员的诉讼至少已经有两起。其中一起是由一名个人股东在旧金山联邦法院提起的拟议集体诉讼，被告包括英伟达公司及黄仁勋。诉讼指控双方涉嫌证券欺诈，认为他们误导了投资者。证券欺诈案件的原告必须证明，英伟达和黄仁勋明知相关陈述具有误导性却仍然向投资者作出；投资者依据这些陈述进行投资；而这些误导性陈述人为推高了英伟达股价。此次集体诉讼涉及的索赔期间，英伟达股价累计下跌了 20%，对应市值损失约 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.68 万亿元人民币）。证券欺诈案件的赔偿金额并没有简单统一的计算公式，但通常而言，涉及的投资损失越大，最终赔偿金额占总损失的比例可能越低。根据斯坦福大学法学院证券集体诉讼信息中心的数据，迄今规模最大的证券欺诈集体诉讼和解案发生于 2006 年。当时，已经倒闭的能源交易公司安然（Enron）的投资者与多家银行及其他被告达成和解，金额高达 72 亿美元（现汇率约合 480.95 亿元人民币）。尽管英伟达没有为公司自身的证券责任购买保险，但如果黄仁勋个人因相关诉讼承担责任，且英伟达无法代为承担这部分责任，他仍可能获得个人高管责任保险的保障。代表股东的律师乔尔 · 弗莱明（Joel Fleming）表示：“考虑到英伟达市值遭受的巨大损失，黄仁勋个人在依据美国《证券交易法》第 10b-5 条提出的证券欺诈索赔中，理论上面临的个人责任可能远远超过 9.5 亿美元（现汇率约合 63.46 亿元人民币）。不过，原告显然会首先尝试向英伟达公司追偿。”这笔 9.5 亿美元（现汇率约合 63.46 亿元人民币）的保险额度，在第二起诉讼中可能发挥更重要的作用。第二起案件是一宗所谓的股东派生诉讼，已在加利福尼亚州圣何塞联邦法院提起，被告为英伟达董事会成员，诉状指控董事未能履行对公司的监督职责。法律专家认为，如果黄仁勋确实曾向投资者作出虚假陈述，将有可能增强投资者提起的证券欺诈集体诉讼的胜诉依据。黄仁勋和蒂姆 · 泰特均已同意于 12 月初接受美国众议院多个委员会的正式录音文字问询。不过，如果董事会是在发现黄仁勋误导公司高管后才决定将其免职，这一行为可能为董事会在股东派生诉讼中提供法律保护，因为这表明董事已经采取行动应对问题。股东派生诉讼旨在追究董事因涉嫌损害公司利益而应承担的责任。相关损失可能包括证券欺诈集体诉讼最终达成的和解金额，以及法院判处的罚款或其他处罚。与证券欺诈集体诉讼不同，股东派生诉讼追回的款项归公司所有，而不是直接支付给股东。此类案件的和解金几乎总是由保险支付，但也有少数特殊情况会让董事个人承担巨额损失。例如，特斯拉董事

articles.title: CoreWeave CEO 因特拉托尔：黄仁勋离开英伟达，我不担心会影响业务
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据《商业内幕》报道，对于黄仁勋离开英伟达会给公司业务带来多大影响，新兴云服务商（或称“新云服务商”） CoreWeave 的 CEO 迈克尔 · 因特拉托尔似乎并不担心。当地时间 17 日，在 Semafor 举办的“硅谷与世界”活动上，因特拉托尔谈及双方的合作关系时显得相当淡定。他认为，英伟达是一家了不起的公司，拥有成千上万名优秀的工程师和员工，这些人仍会与 CoreWeave 保持合作，“每天都有数千名英伟达员工与 CoreWeave 团队协作，处理设备部署、数据中心建设、基础设施网络搭建等工作。这些合作都会继续下去。”主持人接着问，黄仁勋离开英伟达后，CoreWeave 在为数据中心基础设施寻求融资时，是否会感受到他的缺席带来的影响，哪怕只是心理层面的影响。IT之家注；黄仁勋也是 CoreWeave 等新云服务商的重要支持者。对此，因特拉托尔认为，黄仁勋是一位有远见的领导者，他支持的不只是英伟达自身，还有整个数据中心和 AI 产业生态。黄仁勋之所以大力扶持这一生态，是因为供应链中的这些环节过去不可或缺，未来也仍然不可或缺。英伟达将继续支持这些环节，其雄厚的资产负债实力也会继续为它们提供支撑。所谓新云服务商（neocloud），是专门面向 AI 客户提供云计算服务的企业。这类企业去年 10 月因大量举债建设 AI 算力设施而受到关注，但巨额投入最终能带来多少回报，仍是个未知数。投资者对此感到不安，新云服务商的股价也因此大幅下跌。黄仁勋在英伟达任职期间曾多次强调，市场对 AI 云基础设施的需求极其旺盛。英伟达不仅是 CoreWeave、Nebius 和 Iren 等新云服务商的重要供应商，也是它们的重要支持者。

articles.title: 消息称黄仁勋曾力推 RTX 5080 24GB 显卡安抚游戏玩家，如今英伟达或将其取消
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，黄仁勋突然离职后，许多玩家担心，失去黄仁勋掌舵的英伟达可能会进一步向 AI 业务倾斜，而牺牲游戏显卡业务。爆料人士 Moore's Law Is Dead（以下简称 MLID）最新披露的一则消息，似乎印证了玩家的担忧：黄仁勋此前曾希望推出一款高端 RTX 5080 显卡，作为给游戏玩家的“安慰”，以弥补 RTX 5090 价格过高、普通玩家难以负担的问题。MLID 在 YouTube 最新一期《Broken Silicon》播客节目中透露了这一消息，他讨论了近期有关 RTX 5080 24GB 显卡可能取消的传闻。据称，由于 GDDR7 显存芯片价格高昂，这款显卡的推出计划可能已经搁浅。MLID 援引一位英伟达内部消息人士的说法称，RTX 5080 24GB 是黄仁勋亲自推动推出的产品，目的是在英伟达事实上将 RTX 5090 排除在普通游戏玩家的购买范围之外后，至少为玩家提供一款更有吸引力的高端显卡。MLID 表示，英伟达董事会原本并不打算推出 RTX 5080 16GB，也不希望推出 RTX 5080 24GB，甚至不希望 RTX 5090 面向游戏玩家销售。但黄仁勋认为，公司总得给游戏玩家提供一些选择。因此，随着黄仁勋意外辞职，英伟达可能会取消 RTX 5080 24GB，继续保留现有的 16GB 版本，并将其作为 RTX 50 系列事实上定位最高的游戏显卡。不过，MLID 的一位零售渠道消息人士透露，零售商目前已经观察到 RTX 5080 16GB 的供货情况有所改善。这表明，至少这款 16GB 版本仍将继续销售。库存供应略有改善，并不意味着 RTX 5080 16GB 的售价有所下降。目前，这款显卡在 Newegg 上的售价仍在 2,000 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 13,360 元人民币）左右，在亚马逊上的售价则超过 2,000 美元。对于想要组装一台搭载 RTX 5080 的游戏电脑的消费者来说，购买已经预装 RTX 5080 的整机似乎是更合适的选择。

articles.title: 孙正义坦言未投资 Anthropic 是个“错误”，软银对此深感遗憾
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据日经亚洲报道，软银集团创始人孙正义周三表示，早年错过投资 Anthropic 的机会是他所犯的“错误”之一，并对自己在追逐人工智能雄心时选择押注竞争对手 OpenAI 的决定表示遗憾。“当我亲自见到（Anthropic 创始人）达里奥 · 阿莫迪时，我觉得他非常了不起，”孙正义在东京举行的活动上说道，“我真希望当时投了资。”孙正义透露，软银曾探讨过投资 Anthropic 的可能性，但当时已决定支持 OpenAI，并已开始向该公司投入资金。“当时的想法是，不应该‘同时追两只兔子’，”他说。尽管承认从投资策略的角度来看，支持多家公司通常是明智之举，但孙正义指出，要建立稳固的合作伙伴关系，有时需要对某一家特定公司投入更多资源。“你必须在某些投资上投入更多权重，否则就无法真正成为合作伙伴，”他说，“要在选择单一合作伙伴与多个合作伙伴之间找到恰当的平衡，并非易事。”“不过，Anthropic 确实是一家非常出色的公司，”他补充道。IT之家注意到，孙正义发表上述言论之际，Anthropic 正准备在本周上市。此次上市备受瞩目，它将考验投资者对人工智能企业的兴趣 —— 尤其是在科技股剧烈波动，且市场对大规模基础设施支出日益担忧的背景下。不过，孙正义驳斥了有关“人工智能热潮已演变为泡沫”的说法。“人工智能才刚刚起步，”他说，“那些称其为泡沫的人，根本没看清重点。”他回忆起 2000 年互联网泡沫破裂后，由于软银当时资金不足，无法继续进行投资，令他深感遗憾。尽管近期人工智能相关股票出现波动，但孙正义认为，现在正是为未来增长奠定基础的时刻。“幸运的是，这一次我们拥有一定的财务回旋余地，”他在谈及软银的投资能力时表示。与此同时，孙正义还为软银“以投资为主导”的模式进行了辩护。此前，这种模式曾招致批评，有人认为软银本质上不过是一家投资公司而已。“我的目标不是通过投资赚钱，而是通过投资创造未来。”他表示，资本是构建企业的工具，而非终极目的。孙正义指出，软银人工智能战略的四大支柱（模型、芯片、数据中心基础设施以及物理形态的 AI）现已明确，各项筹备工作也已基本就绪。他将这一策略比作日本棋类游戏“黑白棋”（Othello）中占据四个角落的布局，认为这比单纯在某个领域占据主导地位更具优势。这意味着软银需要在整个生态系统中支持多家相互竞争的企业。尽管软银投资了 OpenAI，但孙正义表示，其芯片和数据中心基础设施也应服务于其他 AI 开发者，包括 Anthropic。“如果我们只支持 OpenAI，就无法成为一个平台，”他说。孙正义认为，软银旗下的 Arm 拥有庞大的生态系统，这赋予了该公司独特的优势 —— 能够将强大的数据中心处理器与驱动日常设备中 AI 智能体的各类小型芯片连接起来。在谈及自己的抱负时，孙正义回忆起 17 岁那年看到一张英特尔微处理器照片时所受到的强烈震撼；正是那次经历，激发了他毕生对“信息革命”的追求。他说，如今技术终于发展到了他几十年前所设想的阶段。几年前，他便下定决心将职业生涯的余下时光投入到 AI 领域；因此，他不再关注短期的收益或股价。“真正的好戏现在才刚刚开始，”他说。

articles.title: 英伟达非上市股权投资价值飙升至 655 亿美元，黄仁勋不再掌舵后投资策略成谜
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据外媒 TechCrunch 报道，英伟达持有的非上市公司股权价值持续攀升。当地时间 17 日公布的数据显示，这部分资产目前价值 655 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4,375.31 亿元人民币），较今年 1 月披露的 220 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,469.57 亿元人民币）大幅增加。增长既来自新增投资，也得益于部分现有被投企业估值上调。仅上一季度，英伟达就投入 160 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,068.78 亿元人民币）进行股权投资，本财年前九个月的累计投入更达到 580 亿美元（现汇率约合 3,874.32 亿元人民币）。其中既有对上市公司的股票投资，也有对非上市企业的股权投资。与上一财年相比，英伟达今年明显加大了投资力度。2025 年 11 月，公司披露的上一财年前九个月股权投资额仅为 50 亿美元（现汇率约合 333.99 亿元人民币）。不过，黄仁勋离开管理岗位、由临时 CEO 科莱特 · 克雷斯接任后，英伟达是否还会维持如此大规模的投资，仍是未知数。英伟达在 2023 年末曾明确提出，公司投资初创企业是为了扩大 AI 生态，重点支持能够改变行业格局、创造新市场的企业。据 PitchBook 统计，近三年来，英伟达已投资近 350 家初创企业，投资对象涵盖 Anthropic、OpenAI 等 AI 公司，Thinking Machines 和 Reflection 等新兴 AI 实验室，Lambda、Nscale 和 Crusoe 等新型云服务商，以及 AI 基础设施、机器人和应用开发领域的其他初创企业。除了投资初创公司，英伟达也在为数据中心建设提供大量资金支持。公司披露的担保总额达到 1,180 亿美元（现汇率约合 7,882.24 亿元人民币），其中 1,050 亿美元（现汇率约合 7,013.86 亿元人民币）用于为 OpenAI 在俄亥俄州的 5,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 3.34 万亿元人民币）数据中心项目提供兜底担保。英伟达此前通过动用相当一部分超额现金流来支持上述投资和融资承诺。克雷斯在财报电话会上表示，公司会继续为优质客户提供融资支持，但随着市场逐渐成熟、融资渠道不断增加，英伟达将严格评估未来的投资、承诺和担保。风险投资行业更关心的，是黄仁勋不再掌舵后，英伟达还会不会像过去一样积极扶持初创企业。据报道，黄仁勋频繁进行大规模投资的做法一直让克雷斯颇为担忧。多名投资者向 TechCrunch 透露，他们预计克雷斯会收紧初创企业投资策略，不仅会更加严格地筛选新投资项目，也会减少对现有被投企业的资金支持。克雷斯还透露：“在本财年最后一个季度及今后，我们打算将扣除战略用途后的全部超额自由现金流返还给股东。”

articles.title: 一汽拟利用欧洲闲置产能生产红旗，大众回应称未与一汽讨论欧洲造车合作
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，针对红旗可能与大众汽车合作在欧洲生产汽车的报道，大众中国新闻发言人向观察者网表示：“大众汽车与一汽集团并未就在欧洲生产汽车开展讨论。”IT之家注意到，路透社曾于当地时间 11 月 17 日发文，称一位高管透露，红旗正计划在欧洲本土生产汽车，目前正在评估包括斯特兰蒂斯（Stellantis）和大众汽车在内的多家潜在本地合作伙伴。在意大利威尼斯举行的红旗 EHS4 发布活动上，负责一汽国际业务及红旗欧洲市场拓展的一汽高管肖肖表示，包括本土制造在内的欧洲本地化战略是公司的优先事项。“这无疑是我们正在推进的路径之一，”肖肖表示，“既然我们的口号是‘在欧洲，为欧洲（in Europe, for Europe）’，那么实现运营本地化就至关重要。”肖肖拒绝透露具体的潜在生产基地或其他合作方名称，但他明确表示，相比于收购或自建总装厂，红旗更倾向于借助欧洲车企现有工厂开展合作。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，索尼已经确认，玩家想要在 PS5 上运行即将发售的《GTA 6》，必须先安装近期推出的 PS5 系统固件 14.23 更新。Rockstar Games 也转发了索尼在社交媒体上发布的相关消息。当地时间 11 月 17 日，索尼发布了 PS5 系统软件更新 26.07-14.23.00，安装包大小为 1.267 GB。根据索尼官方更新说明，此次更新主要是对系统软件进行了一些安全修复。如今，距离《GTA 6》于 11 月 19 日午夜在全球陆续解锁仅剩数小时，PlayStation 美国官方客服 X（原 Twitter）账号终于证实了此前外界的猜测。官方表示：“索尼互动娱乐（Sony Interactive Entertainment）已发布一项 PS5 系统软件更新，玩家必须安装该更新才能游玩《GTA 6》。请在 11 月 19 日午夜之前下载并安装更新，以确保能够在游戏发售当天正常游玩。”外界认为，此次不同寻常的 PS5 更新可能会限制旧版系统访问 PlayStation Network（PSN）。这意味着，如果玩家没有将系统升级到 14.23 版本，就无法在 PS5 上游玩《GTA 6》。值得注意的是，此次 14.23 版本更新发布的前一天，一名颇具影响力的 PS5 破解研究人员曾声称，自己是首位在 14.22 版本系统上成功提取游戏二进制文件的人。不过，对方并未公开任何越狱工具。IT之家注意到，过去两个月，PlayStation 自制软件社区（Homebrew）多次发布 PS5 越狱方案。例如，9 月下旬，一款支持运行 7.00 至 13.60 固件版本的 PS5 主机越狱方案震动了整个自制软件社区。当时，这意味着只要 PS5 主机在此前一周内没有升级系统，几乎所有符合条件的设备都可能受到影响，其中甚至包括 PS5 Pro。这对索尼而言意义重大，因为越狱后的 PS5 可以被用户修改，甚至可能为电子游戏盗版打开大门，也直接威胁到 PS5 的系统安全。不过，随后有玩家发现，部分 PS5 游戏已经要求系统升级至更新的 14.00 版本才能下载游戏更新。这也让破解社区重新将目标转向针对新版系统软件开发越狱方案。由此形成了一场类似“打地鼠”的攻防战：自制软件社区不断尝试破解最新的 PS5 固件，而索尼每推出一个旨在加强安全防护的新版本，破解者就不得不重新寻找漏洞，再次展开攻关。这也引发了另一层担忧：假如破解者最终能够针对《GTA 6》运行所必需的固件版本开发越狱工具，那么 Rockstar 的这款游戏就有可能在 PS5 平台遭到盗版，甚至可能进一步通过非官方渠道出现在 PC 平台。对于索尼而言，真正的问题在于，能否最终在这场与自制软件社区的攻防战中占据上风。这关系到索尼主机平台的长期安全，因为游戏发行商和开发商都依赖 PlayStation 平台保护旗下游戏作品。随着能力越来越强大的 AI 模型出现，这一问题也变得更加棘手。就在上周，Rockstar 母公司 Take-Two Interactive 首席执行官斯特劳斯 · 泽尔尼克（Strauss Zelnick）接受 IGN 采访时表示，公司正在认真应对安全威胁，并强调玩家更愿意按照 Rockstar 原本的设计，通过官方渠道体验《GTA 6》的完整内容，而不是选择一个非官方 PC 版本。在一场面向投资者的问答活动中，泽尔尼克被多次问及 AI 可能带来的逆向工程问题。他再次对此作出强硬回应，并暗示 Take-Two 已准备好通过法律手段维护自身权益。泽尔尼克表示：“长期以来，由于游戏文件体积庞大、盗版过程复杂，以及游戏需要连接服务器等原因，我们所在的行业基本上一直不太容易受到盗版问题的影响。毫无疑问，由于技术限制，想要完整复刻玩家按照我们的设计方式体验游戏的整个过程，将会非常困难。不过，正如你所说，这一问题未来会变得更加严峻，我们对此也有充分认识。因此，我们正全力加强技术防御，并在适当情况下强化法律层面的应对措施。当然，我们并不是对此掉以轻心，但所有娱乐行业都不可避免地会受到一定程度的盗版影响。这种情况很可能会以不同程度蔓延到我们的业务中。我认为这一问题是可以控制的，公司也正在积极应对。”

articles.title: 路虎卫士松赞朝圣之路联名版上市：限量发售 20 台，售价 79.88 万元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，路虎卫士与高端度假品牌松赞合作，推出了卫士松赞朝圣之路联名版车型。新车全球限量发售 20 台，官方建议零售价为 79.88 万元，目前已开放预订，意向客户需支付 3 万元定金。IT之家注意到，作为一款面向高原长途穿越场景打造的特别版车型，新车将多项原厂远征装备列为标准配置，包括车顶行李架、折叠式侧梯、20 英寸钻石切割轮圈、专业越野轮胎以及隐藏式电动拖钩，用户无需后期改装即可踏上长途旅程。外观配色以高原岩壁为设计灵感，推出“峡谷红”与“陨石黑”两款专属车漆，并配备联名版专属的原厂哑光保护膜，在营造高级质感的同时具备自愈防刮性能。设计细节上，车身前后的 DEFENDER 字标、C 柱饰板及专属铭牌均采用铜色饰件点缀，其美学灵感取自高原传统手工铜器以及古老建筑历经岁月洗礼后呈现的温润质感。内饰方面，副驾饰板上通过高精度激光蚀刻工艺呈现了松赞专属徽标，进一步强化了联名车型的独特身份。动力方面，联名版车型搭载 3.0T 发动机，最大功率 400 马力。配合第二代智能全地形反馈适应系统（Terrain Response）与电子空气悬架，并拥有 900 毫米的最大涉水深度，无论是高原碎石路面还是陡坡路况，都能提供出色的通过性能。

Isn't this the root of AI psychosis for most? Isn't autocomplete turned conversational just sycophancy for our delusions even if we have guardrails in place?Don't you think that if you can't explain the functionality of an AI model that means you probably shouldn't use it?If you said yes to any of the above I'd love to hear your thoughts on the current state of things. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. articles.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). articles.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. articles.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. articles.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. articles.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. articles.content:

Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. articles.content:

Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. We propose a correction audit, a reproducible evaluation protocol that separates these explanations: it splits each correction into harm and useful gain on identical events, separates the starting prediction from the correction response, and compares objectives with amplitude baselines matched in source harm. articles.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21688v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21691v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rise of mobile devices equipped with numerous sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, has driven the adoption of multi-modal deep intelligence for distributed sensing tasks, such as smart cabins and driving assistance. However, the arrival time of mobile sensory data vary due to modality size and network dynamics, which can lead to delays (if waiting for slow data) or accuracy decline (if inference proceeds without waiting). Moreover, the diversity and dynamic nature of mobile systems exacerbate this challenge. In response, we present a shift to \textit{opportunistic} inference for asynchronous distributed multi-modal data, enabling inference as soon as partial data arrives. While existing methods focus on optimizing modality consistency and complementarity, known as modal affinity, they lack a \textit{computational} approach to control this affinity in open-world mobile environments. %

Abstract: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21766v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2\tau)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. Abstract: The ocean absorbs almost 30% of anthropogenic CO$_2$ emissions, but quantifying this sink requires estimating surface-ocean CO$_2$ from observations that are sparse in space and time. Abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. Abstract: Open crime data support urban safety analysis but reflect reported incidents rather than the complete distribution of criminal activity, potentially introducing spatial distortions in downstream analysis. Abstract: Curvature-enhanced graph convolutional networks (CGCN) incorporate Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC), grounded in optimal transport theory, into message passing, motivated by the claim that curvature-weighted edges alleviate "over-squashing" at structural bottlenecks. Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) decode by iteratively denoising a full canvas of tokens, so every forward pass runs a per-token sampling and stopping pipeline over the entire canvas-by-vocabulary logits tensor. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in vision-language tasks; yet, whether they maintain consistent understanding of information-rich visuals (InfoVis) when the surface language changes remains unclear. To quantify this capability, we introduce MInfoVisQA, a parallel benchmark with 8,960 QA configurations derived from 128 seed instances across 24 languages. We construct seed-matched, language-parallel visuals and QA pairs by disentangling numerical-structural data from text and programmatically synchronizing translated labels. We evaluate 25 MLLMs under two settings: Language-Aligned QA (LQA, matching visual-text languages) and Cross-Language QA (XQA, fixed QA language with varying visual languages). The results show that aggregate accuracy masks substantial robustness gaps: two models with comparable mean LQA accuracy (80.4\%) exhibit performance spreads of 7.8 and 20.3 percentage points across languages. articles.title: Limite 1B - Violetto: Technical Report
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Limite 1B - Violetto, a one-billion-parameter model designed for high-throughput mathematical reasoning. Limite is trained from scratch on 237 billion tokens from a carefully curated, mathematics-centric corpus and supports context lengths of up to 131k tokens. Its architecture and training recipe were developed together to maximize reasoning capability while keeping training and inference costs low. Post-training combines knowledge distillation, targeted supervised fine-tuning, and RLVR on a curated curriculum. Limite achieves 94.01% on AIME 2026 and 74.25% on BeyondAIME, placing it among models many times its size on our evaluation suite. The model is deliberately only lightly instruction-tuned: it is intended primarily as a single-turn mathematical solver and as a fast, parallel component of larger systems, rather than as a general-purpose assistant. articles.title: FieldGuide: A Corpus Map for Token-Efficient Agentic Document Exploration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI agents can help journalists explore large document collections. But exploratory workflows can require substantial token use and time, especially when the task is broad and the relevant subquestions are not yet known. This paper introduces FieldGuide, an agent-facing corpus map that organizes a document collection into a topic hierarchy and exposes tools for corpus orientation, scoped search, and bounded reading. I evaluate FieldGuide on five journalistic document-exploration tasks using 38 Chicago Police Department public-records documents, comparing it with raw-file access and retrieval-augmented generation. Across the five tasks, FieldGuide used 27% fewer tokens and 41% less elapsed time than raw-file access; relative to RAG, it used 38% fewer tokens and 21% less elapsed time. articles.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hoel (2021) proposed that dreams distort replayed experience so that the brain does not overfit to recent events. We test this hypothesis on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5) that stores what it learns in a text memory and rewrites that memory each night from the day's conversation transcript. The agent goes through ten simulated days of conversation built from LongMemEval. We corrupt 5, 10, 20 or 40 percent of the transcript's turns before each nightly rewrite in one of two ways. Detail corruption changes one or two details in a turn to plausible wrong ones, or replaces the turn with one by the same speaker from an earlier day. Random-text corruption replaces half of the selected turns with a passage of Moby-Dick and inserts Moby-Dick words into the other half. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21649v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative approach to human evaluation of literary fictions by employing LLMs themselves as evaluators within the GrAImes framework. We apply this methodology to assess human-written and AI-generated microfictions in Spanish, to five PhD professors in literature and sixteen literary enthusiasts, and to short stories in both Spanish and English. By comparing the evaluations performed by LLMs with those of human judges, we examine the degree of alignment and divergence between both perspectives, thereby assessing the feasibility of LLMs as auxiliary literary evaluators. Our analysis focuses on the alignment of responses from LLMs with those of human evaluators, providing insights into the potential of LLMs in literary assessment. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We study sycophancy as inappropriate agreement: validating a claim, preference, or self-assessment when the context calls for correction, qualification, or resistance. We introduce a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, a persona-targeted evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes with controlled annotations for user openness and stakes. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. First, preference for validating responses in human datasets (Chatbot Arena, HH-RLHF, Community Alignment) is weak and concentrated where agreement is often appropriate. articles.title: Consistency Is Not Correction: Separating Confidence, Abstention, and Recovery in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A controller that resamples an answer, escalates to a larger model, or abstains is usually justified by a confidence signal. Three claims about such a signal do not follow from one another: it ranks answers (discrimination), it supports withholding some of them (selective prediction), and it changes an answer for the better (correction utility). We give an exact decomposition of the third into gated recoveries minus gated harms, which bounds whether a comparison can succeed before it is run: a gate that only replaces a proposal can act only where the base policy was already wrong, so the initial error count caps the discordant pairs any correct gate can produce. When that cap falls below the count a paired test needs, the experiment cannot return a positive result for a working mechanism, nor distinguish one from a gate that never fired. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Financial sentiment analysis is critical for automated trading, portfolio management, and risk assessment, heavily relying on models like FinBERT. Despite high benchmark accuracy, these models remain vulnerable to subtle adversarial text modifications, threatening the integrity of algorithmic decision-making. In this paper, we propose Agent-driven Semantic Inversion (ASI), a novel adversarial attack framework targeting financial sentiment models through domain-specific semantic manipulation. Utilizing an LLM-powered multi-agent pipeline, our approach identifies eligible financial news sentences and applies targeted lexical substitutions. We empirically evaluate ASI against FinBERT, one of the most widely deployed financial sentiment models. articles.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21804v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness. We introduce a controlled bias injection framework that replaces selected agent responses with predefined biased ones, enabling an intervention-based analysis of how network topology and injection configurations shape system behavior. articles.title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. However, existing simulators largely overlook the psychological mechanisms that drive user behavior. We introduce SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors interact to shape user responses. To overcome the challenge of supervising open-ended behavior, we propose a graph reconstruction objective that provides graph-level rewards based on how well simulated conversations reflect the underlying psychological relationships. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations show that SimAI achieves greater simulation and behavioral diversity than existing patient simulators while maintaining strong profile alignment. Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. Existing resources are either synthetically generated from statutory texts, lacking natural information needs, or derived from informal legal question--answer sources without explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents, making them unsuitable for rigorous evaluation of grounded legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. TUSI-Bench is built upon a multi-layered legal knowledge framework containing 7,261 legal articles and integrating codified statutes, legal commentaries, doctrinal writings, and Supreme Court unification rulings. articles.title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21878v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. Such judgments are gradable, carrying both an order and a magnitude. Nearly every benchmark that tests them asks about one entity at a time, then reads that score as the model's knowledge of the domain. Order and magnitude, however, need not be acquired together. Text about social entities carries far more comparison than measurement, so a model may hold a dependable ordering with no anchored scale beneath it. We ask whether a model can place a documented social position on a scale or only order the actors it compares, and what that means for how such knowledge is measured. We test this on party positions in Japan and South Korea, where the Comparative Manifesto Project's coded data supplies a rare external answer key. articles.title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21891v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic assignment of ICD-10 codes from short clinical diagnosis text is a practical medical text classification and normalization task. The task is difficult because diagnosis phrases are short and noisy, the ICD-10 label space is hierarchical, and the class distribution is strongly imbalanced. This paper presents a call-efficient ICD-10 code prediction pipeline that combines transformer embeddings, tree-based supervised candidate generation, candidate-level reranking, and a gated LLM assistance. The evaluation uses a leakage-safe validation protocol: model and threshold selection are based on out-of-fold cross-validation predictions, while final reporting is performed on a locked test set with no shared source-file groups. The supervised conditional parent-code candidate generator reaches 74.32% Top-1 accuracy on the locked test set and 93.05% Top-10 candidate coverage. Abstract: Controlled studies of latent two-hop reasoning train transformers to predict only the answer, whereas language models are trained to predict every token. articles.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency. Abstract: Activation steering is a simple, training-free way to modulate LLM behavior, yet existing methods typically inject vectors at a single layer and lack mechanisms for depth-aware propagation or internal verification. We combine two recent ideas - Attention Residuals (AttnRes) providing learnable cross-layer pathways, and Jacobian-lens (J-space) concept readout - into a lightweight depth-aware steering pipeline. On two small open models (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B), distributing a persona vector according to AttnRes-style depth weights yields stronger internal alignment (deeper-layer concept cosine and rank, p<0.0001) and stronger behavioral shifts than single-layer injection. The effect is sign-specific: reverse vectors invert all six metrics, random directions degrade alignment (p<0.0001), and a short LoRA fine-tune erases the imprint. Abstract: Building integrated photovoltaic power forecasting is challenging because facade orientation, rooftop geometry, nearby buildings, vegetation, cloud movement, module temperature, inverter status and edge device reliability jointly affect power generation. Abstract: The EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 benchmarks egocentric multimodal intelligence linking first-person perception, social reasoning, and interactive action. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Play is used as an indicator of positive welfare in dairy calves, but openly available video of group-housed calves with individual behaviour annotations is scarce. We describe video from four camera deployments of about one week each in group pens of dairy calves on two farms in the Netherlands: a research and teaching dairy farm (2024 and 2025) and a commercial dairy farm (2024). The recordings comprise 1,173 video files spanning 651 h. articles.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression. Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21802v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compressing 3D shapes is important for the efficiency of many applications, yet existing methods either cannot leverage dataset-level statistics or use a fixed compression ratio for all shapes. We propose a learned variable-length compression method that exploits structure across a training dataset while adapting compressed representation size to individual shape complexity using only fast feed-forward inference. Our method operates on general latent representations and improves rate-distortion for both meshes and signed distance fields. Code is available at https://github.com/voilalab/varlen-3D.

articles.content:

Abstract: Multimodal models increasingly reason by synthesizing pixels, sketching maze paths within interleaved chains of thought or rolling out video solutions frame by frame. We study how to allocate test-time compute along two axes: when to render visual thoughts rather than thinking in text or answering directly, and how many denoising steps each thought requires. Causal thoughts carry the plan and become legible early: an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step render in accuracy, commits to the same plan as often as two independent full renders agree, and in video models mostly fails by stalling short of the goal, so the rollout abstains. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21816v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Perceptual similarity metrics for natural images transfer poorly to remote sensing (RS), where severe geospatial and semantic failures can remain visually plausible while still being decisively wrong for downstream use. To address this, we develop a novel human-aligned perceptual quality metric for generated RS imagery and evaluate it across several generation tasks. We first conduct a controlled perturbation study where we progressively increase the severity of common synthetic perturbations. Using the layer-wise Aligned Attention Score (AAS) responses in RemoteCLIP, we find that different RS artifacts are best captured at different depths. Based on these findings, we introduce Remote Sensing Perceptual Distance (RSPD), a pairwise metric that averages seven independently calibrated layer distances without tuning on human-preference labels. articles.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21846v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deepfake detectors often perform well on the dataset they are trained on, but their performance drops when tested on videos from different datasets. In this paper, we study whether a predictive video model can provide a signal that generalizes better across datasets. articles.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21851v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. Abstract: High-resolution facial datasets with consistent UV-mapped geometry, albedo, and physically based displacement are scarce, yet such assets are essential for photorealistic digital-human rendering. arXiv:2611.21890v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physically based facial assets require 4K albedo and displacement maps for cinematic close-ups, yet generative pipelines commonly produce them at only 1K. Naively applying photographic super-resolution is a poor fit: facial UV maps have domain-specific statistics, and displacement is a scalar height field whose errors directly distort geometry. Abstract: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. Re-scoring the same files through a realistic front end costs a standard transfer attack 56% of its dodging protection and a budget-allocating attack 7%, with no image regenerated. Abstract: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke. Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are vulnerable to adversarial visual perturbations, while defenses often require task-specific adversarial fine-tuning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. We propose a passage-focused framework combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. Abstract: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. Abstract: Single-point linearization provides a computationally efficient basis for optimization-based trajectory planning of nonlinear robot manipulators. Abstract: This paper argues that the robotics and AI community should adopt disclosure standards for demonstration videos. articles.title: ImpedanceMimic: Learned Impedance as Action Space for Force-Accurate Motion Imitation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19153v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: different controllers can reproduce the same movement while generating different contact forces. Physics-based motion imitation resolves this ambiguity through simulation, but relies on fixed-gain proportional-derivative (PD) control. We show that fixed gains impose a trade-off between motion and force tracking, as contact and swing place conflicting demands on joint stiffness and damping. We introduce ImpedanceMimic, a reinforcement-learning policy that modulates per-joint stiffness, damping, and position setpoints from motion and force measurements, but requires only motion at inference. Across 129 participants and six activities, ImpedanceMimic outperforms matched fixed-gain PD under every integration scheme, direct-torque, muscle-actuated and existing imitation controllers in kinematic and force fidelity, approaching a dedicated motion-to-force regressor. articles.title: Distilling Safety Filters for Filter-free Multi-agent RL
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19190v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can teach robot teams to navigate shared spaces, but trial and error causes collisions that real robots cannot afford. Control barrier function (CBF) safety filters prevent these collisions by correcting unsafe actions, yet in a team the filter becomes a centralized optimization whose number of constraints grows quadratically with the team size. We propose an approach that builds the filter's safety into the RL policy and examine how such a system behaves during filter-free deployment. However, the filter that keeps training safe also hides what the policy must learn: it masks the cost of unsafe actions, which actor-critic methods then overvalue, and it keeps near-collision states out of the training data. Our approach therefore learns only from executed safe actions with implicit Q-learning and distills the filter into the policy at synthetic near-collision states. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19198v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In simulation, Vision-Agent-Action (VAA) performs pick-and-place in robot cells with gripper or base-frame changes without robot demonstrations or fine-tuning. It uses pre-trained vision-language and language models for interpretation, measures the command map and camera geometry from its own motion and fingertips, estimates lens distortion, and plans grasps from measured object depth. A controlled study of eight public LIBERO-fine-tuned vision-language-action models (VLAs) varies robot hardware, camera geometry, appearance, and base frame. Gripper and frame changes dominate their losses in the tested fractional design. Across 18 cells with these changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%). articles.content:

Abstract: Intent-driven exoskeleton control needs a continuous, causal estimate of the wearer's joint kinematics and an answer to a second question: whose data should train the estimator for a new user? Borrowing the user's recordings of other activities, or other users' recordings of the same activity, is usually evaluated as "more data" versus "less data," which confounds the information a source carries with the optimizer updates it adds and hides negative transfer behind averages. articles.title: Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning for Nonstationary Robot Dynamics
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning about what an action will cause requires internalizing how a system behaves. As conditions seldom stay fixed, this must often happen within a few interactions. Yet systems that look identical in a snapshot can respond differently to the same action, depending on physical conditions the snapshot hides. Context-based models capture this separation by summarizing recent transitions into a latent context, but do not specify how that context should change the equations of motion. Physics-informed neural networks build those equations into the model, but describe only a single system and cannot recognize when it has changed. We present Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges the two. articles.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19274v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. articles.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
articles.content: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones. The temperature hyperparameter controls the level of trust in the pre-trained model, with the limit $T\to \infty$ reverting back to regular SFT and $T=1$ to knowledge distillation. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms standard SFT across domain adaptation, instruction-tuning, and reasoning, leading for up to $21\%$ average relative improvement to standard SFT.

articles.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

articles.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
articles.content: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.

articles.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
articles.content: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.

articles.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
articles.content: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$. To narrow this gap, we propose an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient (SVRG) method that significantly improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Furthermore, when the objective consists of a single function, the proposed method reduces to a novel deterministic first-order method for solving standard convex conic optimization. It achieves a significantly lower gradient evaluation complexity with respect to the objective function compared to existing methods, and can outperform them when computing constraint gradients and projections onto the associated cone is cheaper than evaluating the objective gradient. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articles.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
articles.content: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.

articles.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
articles.content: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

articles.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
articles.content: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 developers who stayed on Opus 4.8 all the time as the control group. We also repeated the comparison across five model upgrades before and after the suspension in 2026 (1,208 developers, 15,442 pull requests). Fitting a difference-in-differences model with developer and date fixed effects, we found that having access to Fable 5 increased the 7-day merge rate of pull requests by only 1.4 percentage points [-1.4; +4.3], which was not statistically significant. Similarly, no significant increases of merge rates were found with the upgrades (weighted mean: -0.9 percentage points [-1.9; +0.2]); all five estimates were negative (95% intervals included 0, did not differ from each other). We also did not observe a significant increase in the number of pull requests merged per week (+2.4% [-4.9%; +10.2%]).

articles.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
articles.content: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC). Results show improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.

articles.title: EviSlide-MIL: Multi-Query Pooling and Shared Prediction for Class-Incremental Whole-Slide Image Classification
articles.content: Histopathological analysis of whole-slide images (WSIs) plays a critical role in cancer diagnosis, and multiple instance learning (MIL) is widely adopted for WSI analysis under weak supervision. As new tumor subtypes are introduced, extending existing MIL models requires learning new classes while retaining knowledge of previously learned ones. This presents a class-incremental learning challenge, where models must acquire new classes with limited access to historical training data and recognize all learned classes without task identifiers at inference. A major obstacle is forgetting, as updates to feature aggregation and prediction modules can degrade performance on previously learned classes. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{EviSlide-MIL}, a class-incremental WSI framework that integrates multiple learnable queries per class with a shared prediction module. The queries aggregate frozen patch features into class-specific representations, while the shared prediction module limits parameter growth across incremental stages. By freezing queries associated with previously learned classes, EviSlide-MIL preserves their attention patterns for identical inputs, while experience replay and knowledge distillation further mitigate forgetting as shared parameters are updated. Experiments on eight tumor subtypes from The Cancer Genome Atlas demonstrate that EviSlide-MIL achieves improved performance and reduced forgetting compared with competing methods across most learning settings, demonstrating its potential for scalable and knowledge-preserving WSI classification. Code and pretrained models will be released.
